references.text: Jesus warns against the scribes and Pharisees who do everything to be seen by people—they wear wide prayer straps, long tassels on their cloaks, love places of honor at banquets, the front seats in synagogues, and being greeted in the marketplaces ([ref:Matt 23:5-7|Matthew 23:5-7]). This is a close parallel to Jesus' warning in Luke 20:46.

The Markan parallel to this verse: Jesus says, 'Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes and be greeted in the marketplaces, and have the front seats in synagogues and places of honor at banquets' ([ref:Mark 12:38-39|Mark 12:38-39]).

Earlier in Luke, Jesus pronounces a 'woe' on the Pharisees because they love the front seats in synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces ([ref:Luk 11:43|Luke 11:43]). The same theme of honor and self-promotion.

Jesus tells a parable about choosing the lowest place at the table instead of a place of honor, urging humility ([ref:Luk 14:7-11|Luke 14:7-11]). This contrasts with the scribes' desire for places of honor at banquets.

In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus warns against doing good deeds to be seen by people ([ref:Matt 6:1-2|Matthew 6:1-2]). The same motif of outward piety and human recognition is found in the criticism of the scribes.

Jesus compares the scribes and Pharisees to whitewashed tombs—beautiful on the outside, but full of impurity and lawlessness inside ([ref:Matt 23:27-28|Matthew 23:27-28]). Their desire to 'walk around in long robes' belongs to that outward appearance which Jesus condemns.

The following verse continues the accusation against the scribes, who devour widows' houses and pray long prayers for show ([ref:Luk 20:47|Luke 20:47]). Together with verse 46, this forms a united judgment on hypocrisy.

Paul urges believers to serve sincerely, not with eye-service as people-pleasers, but as servants of Christ ([ref:Ef 6:6|Ephesians 6:6]). The behavior of the scribes in Luke 20:46 is precisely an example of such eye-service.

Jesus asks, 'How can you believe, since you accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?' ([ref:Joh 5:44|John 5:44]). The scribes' pursuit of greetings and places of honor is exactly an expression of this.

Paul encourages believers to do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves ([ref:Fil 2:3|Philippians 2:3]). This stands in direct contrast to the scribes' desire for prominent positions.
